artworks.title: Pandora
artworks.description: Waterhouse shows Pandora at the moment before catastrophe — the jar still sealed, the gifts of the gods already upon her. The painting trades on the Victorian 'box' afterlife of Hesiod's pithos, but captures the Works and Days portrait of a beautiful evil whose opening will scatter hard toil and sorrow among mankind while Hope stays under the rim.

artworks.title: Pandora (Attic red-figure amphora)
artworks.description: An Attic vase in the British Museum names her ΠΑΝΔΟΡΑ and shows the first woman rising from the earth at the command of the gods — the Hesiodic workshop in which Hephaestus moulds the maiden, Athena dresses her, and Hermes will lead her to heedless Epimetheus as the price of Prometheus' stolen fire.
